title: Jido v3 credential leasing and account setup
destination: Implement credential leasing and provider setup in Jido.Connect. Prove the integration in spikes/connect_bot with optional AshVault and Phoenix support.
acceptance: Prove tenant and resource isolation, durable human delegation, revocation, and secret-free CLI, Phoenix, and reviewed MCP execution. Record the optional package decisions.
target_by: Before the v1 implementation plan is approved
review_by: Review the headless AshVault GitHub CLI spike and unattended authority
authority: The owner authorized implementation and excluded Hozen migration.
notes: Baseline: Connect owns the lease and provider setup contracts. First implementation uses explicit human delegation for unattended runs. Shared service principals, deployment, and publication remain outside this implementation goal.

title: First-release consumers
question: Must v1 serve a handwritten Jido action whose app has no jido_connect dependency?
expected_evidence: Owner selects Connect consumers for v1 or names the first independent consumer and its required behavior.
resolution: Mike Hostetler selected Jido.Connect for v1. Connect owns the lease contract and provider setup. Ash and Phoenix can be optional packages. A standalone credential contract requires a concrete independent consumer.
evidence_refs: Mike Hostetler, 2026-11-22: put this in Jido.Connect
notes: Working recommendation: Connect first; confirm with the owner. This is separate from the choice of repository or umbrella.

title: Authority for unattended runs
question: Which persisted principal may authorize an unattended agent run after the initiating user session has ended?
expected_evidence: Owner selects the first-release grant model: delegated human, scoped service principal, or both. State who can grant and revoke use, and what happens after membership changes.
resolution: Use an explicit grant from an authenticated human who has delegation and use permissions on their tenant-owned binding. The grant owner can revoke it. Removing delegation or use permission invalidates old grants, even if the permission is restored.
notes: The host uses explicit human delegation. It persists membership and permission changes, denies queued work after revocation, and requires a new grant if the principal loses use or delegation access. The CLI keeps one local operator. Tests use the same host interface with two tenants and multiple users. An old-format live GitHub run passed after storage upgrade.

title: Provider setup paths
question: Which setup paths can one provider support through both the headless and web entry points?
expected_evidence: Candidate provider matrix covering key entry, device or other headless authorization, web OAuth callback, refresh, and disconnect. Select a candidate for the proof and identify required registration and permissions.
resolution: Use GitHub for the first proof. Import a personal access token as a key. Use device authorization in the CLI and an authorization-code callback with PKCE in Phoenix. Use refresh when GitHub issues an expiring token pair. Use reconnect if the provider rejects refresh.
notes: Register the OAuth app callback and enable device authorization for the CLI. Request repo scope for the spike action. The device path uses the client ID. The web exchange and refresh use the host-held client secret. The app revokes the local binding on disconnect. The provider exposes OAuth token revocation for hosts that choose remote revocation.

title: Lease execution contract
question: Can a single trusted-context resolver serve the chosen consumers without carrying secrets in persisted execution state?
expected_evidence: Small proof with a generated action and a background run. Check resource denial before secret access, sanitized errors, secret-free persistence, bounded lease expiry, and revoked grants on resumed runs. Inspect the sensor path and include it if v1 requires it.
resolution: Use Jido.Connect.CredentialResolver for direct actions and polling. Persist a grant and binding reference. Recheck both before loading a short-lived lease.
notes: Core tests cover resolver order, refusal without fallback, sanitized failure, and fresh polling leases. The generated GitHub action runs in a durable CLI job. The live smoke passed again through the shared token import API. Prepared mutation approvals retain their explicit lease binding. The reviewed MCP proof is tracked in D7.

title: AshVault authorization boundary
question: Can app-owned Ash resources enforce separate manage, delegate, and use permissions while limiting decryption to the approved runtime path?
expected_evidence: Real AshVault-backed records with two tenants. Prove allowed use and deny other tenant, user, agent and resource. Test authorization before decryption, ordinary reads, revoked grants, and a concurrent OAuth refresh using a single-writer or versioned update.
resolution: Keep Ash policies, tenant key scopes, membership and grant storage in the host. Use a single refresh writer per binding in the local spike. Replace the token pair in one storage transaction for the current binding.
notes: The CLI tests cover two tenant vault scopes, separate role permissions, ordinary reads, and rejection of unauthorized reads before decryption. Two concurrent leases make one refresh request and use the replacement access token. A reconnect during refresh prevents the old result from replacing the new binding. The spike demonstrates single-node refresh.

title: Account setup interface
question: Can one provider flow API support both a CLI and a mounted Phoenix Connections screen with app-owned authentication?
expected_evidence: One API key and one OAuth flow produce grants usable by the same resolver. Prove the CLI path runs without Phoenix. For web OAuth, check provider-specific callback URLs, state replay and wrong-session denial, and reconnect handling.
resolution: Expose Jido.Connect.AccountSetup with provider callbacks for key import, browser OAuth, device OAuth, and refresh. Hosts own authenticated principal selection, atomic one-use state, and credential storage.
notes: The headless app stores imported and OAuth credentials in AshVault and uses the same resolver. Phoenix uses the same setup API with its in-memory host adapter. Tests cover PKCE, callback route and client binding, wrong-session denial, replay, and an earlier callback racing with reconnect. OAuth exchanges used HTTP fixtures.

title: Second execution path
question: Can a reviewed MCP read or the chosen independent consumer use the same grant without weakening execution policy?
expected_evidence: Run one real execution path selected by v1 scope with the same resolver. For MCP, bind an allowed tool and endpoint and check that schema changes and unauthorized calls fail. Keep existing approval rules for generic MCP calls.

title: Package and release boundary
question: Which optional Mix packages should hold the Ash adapter and Phoenix components for the first adopter release?
expected_evidence: Owner accepts a dependency diagram and a release boundary grounded in the two execution paths and both setup modes. Identify a concrete trigger for extracting a standalone contract.
notes: D1 fixes Connect ownership for the lease and provider setup APIs. Use the execution and setup proofs to decide optional package boundaries.

title: Hozen migration
notes: The owner excluded Hozen migration and changes to Hozen from the implementation goal.

title: Hosted credential broker and new identity provider
notes: The first roadmap covers in-process lease resolution and integration with the host's existing sign-in. A separate trust boundary needs a later design.

title: Deployment and publication
notes: The implementation goal covers Jido.Connect and spikes/connect_bot. Deployment, package publication, and release operations are outside its scope.
